# The POD Launch Checklist — 47 Steps to Your First Etsy Sale

### A Complete Print-on-Demand Launch System for New Sellers

---

> **How to use this checklist:** Work through each phase in order. Tick each item only when fully complete — not "good enough." Most sellers who don't make their first sale within 60 days skipped something in Phases 1–3.

---

## PHASE 1: FOUNDATION SETUP
*Complete before designing a single product*

- [ ] **1. Choose your POD supplier** — Pick ONE to start. Printful or Printify for beginners. Gelato if you have EU customers. Don't split focus.

- [ ] **2. Create your supplier account** and connect it to a test Etsy shop (or your real one) to confirm the integration works before you invest time in designs.

- [ ] **3. Research your niche using Etsy search** — Type your niche keyword and note the autocomplete suggestions. These are real buyer searches, not guesses.

- [ ] **4. Validate demand with eRank or Marmalead** — Confirm your target keyword gets at least 1,000 monthly Etsy searches before committing to it.

- [ ] **5. Analyse 10 bestselling listings in your niche** — Note their prices, mockup styles, number of reviews, and listing titles. Screenshot them. This is your benchmark.

- [ ] **6. Identify a sub-niche gap** — Find what those bestsellers *don't* offer. Example: "dog mum" is saturated; "Dachshund mum with sarcastic humour" is specific and winnable.

- [ ] **7. Define your target buyer in one sentence** — e.g., *"Women aged 28–45 who own rescue dogs and follow accounts like The Dodo."* Every design decision filters through this person.

- [ ] **8. Check your niche's seasonality** — Use Google Trends to confirm demand is consistent or rising, not dying. Avoid niches peaking in month 1 of a multi-year decline.

---

## PHASE 2: ETSY SHOP SETUP
*Your shop is a storefront — treat it like one*

- [ ] **9. Create your Etsy seller account** with a professional email address (not your personal Gmail from 2008).

- [ ] **10. Choose a memorable shop name** — Keep it under 20 characters, easy to spell, relevant but not so niche-specific that you can't expand later. Check it's not trademarked.

- [ ] **11. Write your shop announcement** — One paragraph. Who you serve, what makes you different, and a soft CTA. Example: *"Custom gifts for dog lovers who hate boring presents. Made to order, shipped worldwide."*

- [ ] **12. Complete your About section with a real story** — Buyers trust humans. Write 150+ words. Include why you started, even if it's just "I wanted a side income doing something creative."

- [ ] **13. Upload a professional shop banner and logo** — Use Canva. Your banner should visually communicate your niche within 2 seconds. No blurry images. No default placeholders.

- [ ] **14. Set your shop policies** — Cover processing times, returns (POD is typically no-returns unless damaged), and damaged item resolution. Copy Etsy's suggested policies as a starting template, then personalise.

- [ ] **15. Add your payment and billing details** — Obvious, but shops stall here. Confirm Etsy Payments is active in your country.

- [ ] **16. Set realistic processing times** — Check your POD supplier's current production times. Add 2 days buffer. Don't promise 3-day dispatch if your supplier takes 5.

---

## PHASE 3: PRODUCT CREATION
*Where most beginners waste weeks — use this to stay focused*

- [ ] **17. Order a sample of your hero product** — Before listing anything publicly, hold your actual product. Feel the print quality, check the sizing, photograph it. Non-negotiable.

- [ ] **18. Start with ONE product type** — T-shirt, mug, or tote. Master one before diversifying. Spreading across 10 product types immediately kills momentum and focus.

- [ ] **19. Create 3–5 designs maximum for launch** — Quality over quantity. Five well-researched designs beat fifty rushed ones. You can add more after your first sale.

- [ ] **20. Design at the correct resolution** — Minimum 300 DPI for print. Use your supplier's exact template dimensions. Download them from your supplier's asset library.

- [ ] **21. Use licensed or original fonts only** — Google Fonts (check commercial licence), Creative Fabrica with a commercial licence, or fonts you've purchased. Never use fonts downloaded from random sites.

- [ ] **22. Trademark check every phrase and design** — Search USPTO.gov (US) and EUIPO.eu (EU). "This Is Fine" is trademarked. "Dog Mum" variations may be. Check before printing.

- [ ] **23. Design for the actual product colour** — A design that looks great on white may be invisible on black. Test dark and light versions. Use your supplier's mockup generator.

- [ ] **24. Create lifestyle mockups, not just flat lays** — Use Placeit.net or your supplier's mockup tool. Show a real person wearing/using the product in a relevant context.

- [ ] **25. Create 5–8 mockup images per listing** — Lead with a lifestyle image. Include: close-up of design, size chart, product on a model, care instructions visual, and a "gift context" image.

---

## PHASE 4: LISTING OPTIMISATION
*This is where sales are won or lost*

- [ ] **26. Write your listing title using the formula:**
`[Primary Keyword] — [Secondary Keyword] — [Benefit or Occasion]`
Example: *"Dachshund Mum T-Shirt — Funny Dog Owner Gift — Birthday Gift for Her"*

- [ ] **27. Front-load your most important keyword** — Etsy's algorithm weights the first few words heavily. Don't start with your shop name or filler words.

- [ ] **28. Write a description that sells, not just describes** — Open with a buyer-focused benefit sentence. Example: *"Know someone obsessed with their Dachshund? This is the only gift they actually want."* Then cover specs, sizing, care, and delivery.

- [ ] **29. Use all 13 tags — every single one** — Each tag is a search opportunity. Mix exact phrases ("funny dog shirt"), broad terms ("gift for dog lover"), and long-tail ("dachshund owner birthday gift").

- [ ] **30. Set a competitive price — not the cheapest** — Find the average price of your top 10 competitors. Price at the average or 10% above if your mockups are better. Cheapest price signals low quality.

- [ ] **31. Offer multiple variants strategically** — For t-shirts: include at least 5 colours. For mugs: offer 11oz and 15oz. More variants = more chances to match a buyer's preference.

- [ ] **32. Fill in all product attributes** — Colour, size, material, occasion, recipient. These feed into Etsy's filter system and category pages. Blank fields are missed traffic.

- [ ] **33. Enable free shipping (US domestic at minimum)** — Etsy's algorithm favours free shipping listings. Build the shipping cost into your product price. A £18 mug with free shipping outperforms a £14 mug with £4 shipping.

- [ ] **34. Set the correct category and subcategory** — Drill down to the most specific category available. "Clothing > Tops & Tees > Graphic Tees" beats "Clothing."

- [ ] **35. Add a size guide in your images AND description** — Sizing questions are the #1 reason buyers abandon POD listings. Remove this objection proactively.

---

## PHASE 5: PRE-LAUNCH CHECKLIST
*Final checks before going live*

- [ ] **36. Place a test order through your own shop** — Confirm the checkout process, variant selection, and supplier connection all work correctly. Fix any errors before real buyers find them.

- [ ] **37. Preview every listing on mobile** — Over 60% of Etsy traffic is mobile. Check images look sharp, title isn't cut off, and the description is scannable with short paragraphs.

- [ ] **38. Confirm all listings are set to "Active"** — Rookie mistake. Draft listings don't generate traffic or sales.

- [ ] **39. Set up Etsy offsite ads awareness** — Understand that Etsy auto-enrols you in offsite ads once you reach £10k revenue. This isn't required at launch, but know the terms.

- [ ] **40. Turn on Etsy Ads at $1/day for your top listing** — Even minimal Etsy Ads budget gets your listing impressions while organic SEO builds. Track clicks vs. spend weekly.

---

## PHASE 6: POST-LAUNCH MOMENTUM
*What you do in the first 30 days determines your trajectory*

- [ ] **41. Pin your best listing to Pinterest** — Create a vertical pin (1000×1500px) with your lifestyle mockup and your Etsy listing URL. POD and Pinterest have natural overlap — long buying cycles, visual discovery.

- [ ] **42. Post 3 times in relevant Reddit communities** — NOT to spam. Post genuine value in r/Etsy, r/printondemand, or niche subreddits (r/DachshundLovers). Mention your shop only where rules allow.

- [ ] **43. Monitor your Shop Stats daily for the first 2 weeks** — Track: views, visits, conversion rate, and which listings get traffic. Data tells you where to double down.

- [ ] **44. Identify your "no purchase" listings** — Any listing with 50+ views and zero sales has a problem. Diagnose: Is the price wrong? Are mockups weak? Is the title off? Fix before adding new listings.

- [ ] **45. Message every buyer after purchase** — Send a brief, warm thank-you message. Mention that if anything is wrong, you'll make it right immediately. This pre-empts negative reviews and builds repeat buyers.

- [ ] **46. Request reviews from satisfied customers** — After confirmed delivery, send a short follow-up message. Example: *"Hope your order arrived safely! If you love it, a quick review means the world to a small shop like mine."*

- [ ] **47. Analyse, iterate, and add Listing #6** — Once you have 30 days of data, you know what's working. Your sixth listing should be a variation of your best-performing concept, not a guess.

---

## QUICK REFERENCE: COMMON REASONS FIRST SALES DON'T COME

| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| No traffic | Revisit title tags and add Etsy Ads |
| Traffic but no sales | Improve mockups and add size guide |
| Wrong niche | Validate demand *before* designing |
| Underpriced listings | Raise price — cheap signals low quality |
| Poor mockups | Invest £10 in Placeit subscription |
| Vague descriptions | Lead with buyer benefit, not product specs |

---

## YOUR FIRST SALE TIMELINE (REALISTIC)

- **Days 1–7:** Setup and first 3 listings live
- **Days 8–21:** SEO begins indexing, first Etsy Ads impressions
- **Days 22–45:** First sale typically occurs in optimised shops
- **Days 46–60:** Diagnose and reoptimise any zero-conversion listings
- **Day 60+:** Scale what's working, cut what isn't

---

*Built for POD sellers who want results, not motivation. Return to this checklist every time you add a new product line.*
